analysis:
Reviewed both primary analyses and independently checked the replayed patches, gitlink metadata, and BASE/HEAD StopSequence source against the canonical index and detailed T-041 definition. No supported security regression is established within this evidence.

EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift HEAD 249–250 forwards stopStringScope alongside the unchanged prefix-checkpoint target. EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift HEAD 14–31 applies that scope when identifying the terminating stop string; its nil-scope branch preserves BASE matching behavior. These changes align request submission and stop reporting, but their correctness depends on SDK scope semantics. The visible changes do not modify encryption, attestation, serving authorization, authenticated cache-salt derivation, persistent-cache policy, or billing controls. No new violation of those contracts is demonstrated.

Material uncertainty remains: StopSequence.swift HEAD 30 assumes StopHoldback returns text whose Unicode-scalar length equals the raw prefix preceding the stop. Review StopHoldback, CBv2StopStringScope, scope initialization, translation and event-pump handling together to verify offsets, split channel markers, overlapping stops, analysis/tool exclusion, and consistent streaming versus replay behavior. Confirm token budgets and cancellation still bound generation (A-001, TB-007, T-007, T-010, A-018), and that cache identity and account isolation remain intact (T-041).

All three libs/mlx, libs/mlx-swift and libs/mlx-swift-lm gitlinks change at line 1, but implementation deltas are absent. Review those deltas for native memory safety, plaintext/media handling, cache isolation and availability before reaching a security conclusion. Replay is explicitly incomplete (four source units omitted), so documentation and Submission surrounding-source claims in the prior analyses cannot all be independently verified here. Missing evidence is a coverage limit, not a finding or assurance of safety.
